slides.title: Mobility, Memory, and Network Structure in Agent-Based Models of Convention Tipping and Convergence
slides.highlight: This research on how mobility, memory, and network topology influence the adoption of new conventions is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Mobility is the primary driver accelerating the inevitable tipping of social conventions in networked agent populations.
card.key_idea: A stylized agent-based model using a unified predictive equation to quantify how mobility, memory, and network topology determine the time to full convention adoption.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 21,600 simulation samples across 432 configurations. The predictive model achieved R² = 0.91 and RMSE ≈ 57, outperforming simpler nested baselines.
card.limitation: The model is a theoretical, stylized mechanism-oriented simulation rather than an empirical predictor of specific real-world social systems.

slides.title: Designing Social Robots for Inclusive Child Wellbeing Assessment: Insights from Communities Supporting Developmental Language Disorder and Forced Migration
slides.tldr: INCLUSIVE SOCIAL ROBOT DESIGN FOR CHILD WELLBEING ASSESSMENT
slides.highlight: This research provides design recommendations for using social robots to assess the wellbeing of children with communication barriers, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Stakeholder insights for designing inclusive social robot interactions to assess wellbeing in children with communication barriers.
card.key_idea: Used design probes and focus groups with parents and professionals to derive ethical, inclusive recommendations for robot-mediated assessment for children with DLD and forced migration backgrounds.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of focus group discussions with 14 stakeholders (parents and professionals) across two specific vulnerable child populations.
card.limitation: The study is a qualitative design phase; it does not yet test the robot interactions directly with children.

slides.title: How Should I Pick a Foundation Model for My Robot? In Favor of a Community Evaluation Framework for Social Robots
slides.tldr: EVALUATION FRAMEWORK FOR SOCIAL ROBOT FOUNDATION MODELS
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a three-tiered evaluation funnel and five key dimensions to help researchers select foundation models for social robots, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A proposed three-tiered evaluation funnel to help researchers select foundation models for social robots.
card.key_idea: Filters models through curated static benchmarks (T1), simulated interactions with LLM users/judges (T2), and robot-specific hardware evaluation (T3) across five key social dimensions.
card.evaluation: Proposed as a conceptual framework and case study (Haru robot); no new empirical results are reported.
card.limitation: Multimodal interaction integration, the boundary between harness replay and live user studies, and cross-platform harness abstraction remain unresolved.

slides.title: SAIN: Structure-Aware Interactive Navigation with Active Dialogue Grounding for Mobile Robot
slides.highlight: SAIN converts active dialogue into persistent navigation states to resolve ambiguous human instructions, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction in embodied learning.

card.one_liner: SAIN converts active dialogue into persistent structured memories for zero-shot interactive instance goal navigation.
card.key_idea: A dialogue-to-state framework that compiles oracle answers into target evidence, route-level corridor memories, and object-candidate labels to guide frontier ranking and target approach.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VL-LN IIGN benchmark; improved SR from 20.2 to 25.4 and SPL from 13.07 to 14.17 over the strongest dialogue-enabled baseline.
card.limitation: Ambiguity remains the primary failure bottleneck, accounting for 51.2% of failed episodes in the SAIN-D setting.

slides.title: Deep Learning for Real-Time Sound Order Recognition in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research introduces a deep learning framework to recognize the temporal order of overlapping sounds, supporting the HRI goals of RwB.

card.one_liner: A deep learning framework for real-time recognition of the temporal order of overlapping non-verbal sounds.
card.key_idea: Multi-branch CNN processing Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, and STFT features, utilizing an attention-based fusion mechanism to identify critical temporal cues.
card.evaluation: Tested on balanced, varied-amplitude, and unseen sounds; achieved 99%, 91%, and 74% accuracy respectively, with real-time latency benchmarks.
card.limitation: Experiments relied on carefully controlled synthetic overlaps, posing challenges for ecological validity in real-room environments.

slides.title: Human Centric Embodied Intelligence for Soft Wearable Robotics
slides.tldr: HUMAN-CENTRIC EMBODIED INTELLIGENCE FOR SOFT WEARABLES
slides.highlight: This review proposes a framework for Human-Centric Embodied Intelligence (HCEI) in soft wearable robots, focusing on the integration of sensing, cognition, and human adaptation. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposes a human-centric framework for integrating intelligence and adaptation into soft wearable robotic systems.
card.key_idea: The Perception-Cognition-Actuation-Augmentation (PCAA) framework shifts design from actuator-first to perception and cognition-driven, focusing on the coupled human-robot system's emergent intelligence.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; this is a review paper synthesizing existing advances rather than an empirical study.

slides.title: From Speech to Interaction: Analyzing Multimodal Systems in Cocktail-Party Scenarios
slides.tldr: ANALYZING MULTIMODAL SYSTEMS FOR COCKTAIL-PARTY SCENARIOS
slides.highlight: This work analyzes audio-visual systems for recognizing speaker groups and transcribing conversations in cocktail-party scenarios, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and diarization.

card.one_liner: Analysis of multimodal systems for cocktail-party scenarios shows that AVSR modeling drives performance more than speech separation.
card.key_idea: Evaluates three strategies for multi-talker recognition: audio-visual target speech separation, improved AVSR backbones, and LLM-based semantic clustering for grouping speakers into conversations.
card.evaluation: Tested on CHiME-9 MCoRec dataset using WER, Clustering F1, and JointError; best system achieved 57% relative error reduction.
card.limitation: Semantic clustering depends on transcription quality, and visual interaction cues (like gaze) generalize poorly to evaluation sets.

slides.title: Robot Learning from Human Demonstrations: Handwritten Alphabet Trajectories and Human-Likeness Evaluation
slides.tldr: LEARNING HUMAN-LIKE ROBOT MOTION FROM HANDWRITING
slides.highlight: This work presents a framework for learning human-like robot motion from handwriting demonstrations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A framework for learning human-like robot handwriting using an extended GMM+GMR approach and a new dataset.
card.key_idea: Extends GMM+GMR by incorporating contact force and normalized time dimensions, using a segment-detection step to handle non-continuous, multi-stroke trajectories from human demonstrations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a user study (21 participants) using a 0-100 human-likeness scale; generated trajectories scored 71.50, indicating perceived human-likeness.
card.limitation: Evaluations used a simulated robot rather than physical hardware; sample sizes were small and demonstrations followed predefined guidelines.

slides.title: DOBOT Unveils All-Terrain Humanoid Robot LUMO
slides.tldr: ALL-TERRAIN HUMANOID ROBOT WITH VR TELEOPERATION
slides.highlight: The introduction of the LUMO all-terrain humanoid robot and its VR teleoperation capabilities is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: DAVE: A Decoupled Audio-Visual Enhancement Framework for Real-World Speech Separation
slides.highlight: DAVE introduces a decoupled framework and a large-scale corpus to improve speech separation and speaker identity preservation under visual degradation. This supports HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and identity recognition in challenging environments.

card.one_liner: DAVE is a decoupled audio-visual framework improving speech separation robustness against unreliable visual inputs.
card.key_idea: Uses a large-scale augmented corpus (DAVE-Corpus), progressive multi-objective optimization, and a certified selective enhancement chain featuring scene routing and GAN-based denoising.
card.evaluation: Tested on the Real-World Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement Challenge; demonstrated robustness under real-world mixed scenarios and visual degradation.

slides.title: Unichem Acquires Electronic Skin Firm Loomia
slides.highlight: The acquisition of Loomia by Unichem focuses on humanoid tactile sensing, which is relevant to RwB's work on embodied social robots.

slides.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for capturing and transferring contact-rich human bathing demonstrations to robots, contributing to the development of safe physical human-robot interaction (pHRI) relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A framework for capturing and transferring high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to a robot-assisted system.
card.key_idea: Uses contact regions as processing primitives to reconstruct synchronized motion, shape, and force, enabling retargeting to a tendon-driven soft hand and robotic arm.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using a dataset of 128 captures (3 clinicians, 6 subjects) and real-world deployment on a mannequin via open- and closed-loop control.
card.limitation: Substantial sim-to-real gap; closed-loop control uses aggregate pressure sums rather than distributions; not yet ready for human subjects.

slides.title: Graphing the Everyday: A Neurosymbolic Approach to Eliciting Routines for Just-In-Time Adaptive Interventions
slides.highlight: This work explores a neurosymbolic pipeline combining LLMs and knowledge graphs to map verbal narratives into routines, which is relevant to MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic and LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A neurosymbolic pipeline using LLMs and knowledge graphs to translate conversational user routines into JITAI schedules.
card.key_idea: Combines LLM-based conversational elicitation with a Neo4j knowledge graph to map unstructured narratives into structured entities and temporal relations for proactive health interventions.
card.evaluation: Qualitative lab study with 16 participants using member-checking, state-machine traces, and knowledge-graph visualizations to assess representational fidelity.
card.limitation: A 'mental-model gap' exists where linear LLM extraction fails to capture hierarchical, non-linear human storytelling, causing entity fragmentation.

slides.title: PromptShield Home: Ambient Multimodal Prompt Injection Defense for Smart-Home Agents
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL PROMPT INJECTION DEFENSE FOR SMART HOMES
slides.highlight: This work addresses addressee ambiguity and multimodal prompt injection in smart-home agents, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception.

card.one_liner: PromptShield-Home benchmarks multimodal prompt injection in smart homes, finding MLLMs over-refuse while traditional detectors over-execute.
card.key_idea: A comparative framework testing three layers: traditional detectors (L0), single MLLM agents (L1), and multi-agent mediation (L2) across realistic ambient-signal scenarios.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 19 pilot scenarios using unsafe-execution and safe-completion rates; results show complementary failure modes between L0 and MLLMs.
card.limitation: Small benchmark size (N=19), lack of a trained router (uses an oracle), and high VRAM requirements for MLLMs.
